narrative.overview:
BuildLedger is drawn as a single ruled sheet of a finance ledger laid on a Swiss grid, not as a dashboard of cards. Warm paper ground, near-black ink, and 1px rules do the structural work; there are no tinted panels, no card stacks and no shadows on the page. Density is high on purpose: a QS reads eighteen cost codes and nine columns at once, a director reads one large red figure. Both are served by the same sheet because emphasis is rationed, not because content is thinned.

Colour is semantic before it is anything else. One red owns overrun and exceptions; amber owns anything waiting on someone or approaching a statutory clock; green appears only when something is approved or connected. Everything else is ink and graphite. The five source systems each get a quiet, low-chroma hue used only as an outlined tag, so provenance is always present and never louder than status.

Type is one neo-grotesque (Archivo) in tight, small steps with tabular figures everywhere money appears, and one monospace (JetBrains Mono) reserved for identifiers: cost codes, project codes, PO and bill references. The signature component is the budget-to-forecast bridge, which steps from the CostX budget to the forecast at completion one trade at a time. The rest of the app currently inherits these tokens but has not yet been recomposed; the project detail page and the shell are the reference implementation.
keyCharacteristics: One bordered sheet per page, divided by hairline rules; section heads sit on a 1px ink rule.
Red appears only on overrun figures, exception markers and overdue-on-us clocks.
Every key figure has an outlined source tag beside it or in its column header.
Tabular figures throughout; mono only for identifiers.
Near-square corners (1-3px); flat on the page, one shadow for floating layers only.
Light first, with a full warm-dark counterpart driven by the same token names.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Red means over budget or exception, and nothing else. A favourable or zero variance stays graphite (rendered as an em dash when zero), never green.

rules.name: The Provenance Recedes Rule
rules.body: Source tags are outlined in the system's own hue and never filled, never bolder than the figure they annotate; a red overrun must always read before its tag.

rules.name: The Ink Is the Accent Rule
rules.body: There is no brand colour. Primary actions and active states are an ink inversion of the ground.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every money figure, percentage and count is set with tabular numerals (the whole table inherits it) so columns align digit for digit.

rules.name: The Mono Is for Identifiers Rule
rules.body: Mono marks something you could look up in a source system: a code or a reference number. Amounts, labels and headings never use it.

rules.name: The Size of the Question Rule
rules.body: The answer to "how much is this job losing" is set larger than the job's name.

rules.name: The One Sheet Rule
rules.body: Sections of a page are ruled divisions of one sheet, not separate cards with gaps between them.

rules.name: The Ruled Head Rule
rules.body: A section head sits on a 1px ink rule; rows within it are divided by hairlines; a total sits under a 1px ink rule and closes with an accountant's double rule.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the page flow casts a shadow; if a surface needs separating, give it a rule or a tone step.

rules.name: The Near-Square Rule
rules.body: No radius above 3px, and no pill shapes; status reads from colour and words, not from soft lozenges.

dos: Do set every money figure with tabular numerals and right-align it in columns.
Do put an outlined source tag next to every key figure or in its column header, in that system's hue at the tag size.
Do build pages as one bordered sheet divided by hairlines, with section heads on a 1px ink rule.
Do close totals with a 1px ink rule and the 5px double rule.
Do use square markers (6px or 8px) for severity and state, not dots.
Do keep favourable and zero variances graphite, with an em dash for zero.
Do use mono only for codes and reference numbers.
Do honour reduced motion for scroll and panel transitions.
donts: Don't use red for anything other than over budget and exceptions, including selection, brand or emphasis.
Don't use green for a favourable variance; green means approved, paid, met or connected.
Don't fill source tags or give them a status hue.
Don't split a page into a row of KPI cards, chart cards and table cards with gaps between them.
Don't put a shadow on anything in the page flow; the overlay shadow is for menus, tooltips and popovers only.
Don't use corners above 3px or pill shapes, except the round user avatar.
Don't set uppercase tracked labels above headings.
